label: D2 arrival in S2: rare a1->S2 throughout, any S2 arrival late in episode
explanation: Almost all activation (99% of mass) falls on DELAY_2 steps where state S2 is reached (28% of S2 D2 steps fire; it never fires at D1 and almost never on S1 arrivals or at GO). Within S2 arrivals, it fires mainly on rare transitions (a1 chosen, landed in S2: 74% precision there; top activations are all a1->S2 rare). Common a2->S2 arrivals fire only late in the episode (trials 80-99). There is a strong episode-time drift: no firing before trial ~20, and the rate climbs steeply over trials 80-99. Firing also goes with low model value (rate 18% in the lowest value bin, 0 in the highest). Magnitude is largest for rare a1->S2 arrivals. All variables are observed at D2. Episode time is not an input, so the drift probably reflects slow growth of the hidden state. Simpler variants: D2&S2 alone gets F1 0.44 (recall 0.97); D2&S2&(a1 | trial>=85) gets F1 0.83.

issues: The factual claims check out on dev. D1 never fires (0/380619). GO fires at 0.4% (mass 0.006). S1 arrivals at D2 fire at 0.2% (mass 0.0006). 28.2% of S2 arrivals at D2 fire. D2&S2&a1 has precision 0.739, matching the stated 74%. Nothing fires before trial 20: a1->S2 at trials <20 has precision 0.007. Common a2->S2 before trial 80 has precision 0.010. Rates by value bin are 18.4% in the lowest and 0% in the highest. All top activations are a1->S2 rare arrivals.

The original predicate reproduces on test: P 0.775, R 0.949, F1 0.853, mass recall 0.986. Missed activations hold only 1.4% of the mass and are scattered (weak a2->S2 firings before trial 80, a few GO steps).

There is a systematic false-positive class in the a2 (common) arm. 'ep_trial >= 80' is too coarse. Common a2->S2 arrivals fire at 97% precision in trials 90-99, but only 37% in trials 80-89. Within trials >= 80 they also depend on the previous trial's reward, which is shown at D1 and so is observed: precision 0.88 when prev_reward==0 vs 0.53 when prev_reward==1. Most of the predicate's 16k test false positives are a2->S2 arrivals in trials 80-89 after a rewarded previous trial.
Value is not a better explanation on its own. D2&S2&(value<x) peaks at F1 about 0.70, so the low-value correlation is secondary to the action-by-episode-time structure.

Smaller point: in the a1 arm, firing is stronger when S1 is the good state (precision 0.89) and when value is low (value<7.13 gives precision 1.0). The rare-arrival response is largest when the arrival is surprising or bad, which the label does not mention.
